bib.title: TiDAR: Think in Diffusion, Talk in Autoregression

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "TiDAR: Think in Diffusion, Talk in Autoregression", Jingyu Liu*, Xin Dong*, Zhifan Ye, Rishabh Mehta, Yonggan Fu, Vartika Singh, Jan Kautz, Ce Zhang, Pavlo Molchanov (NVIDIA), arXiv 2511.08923v1 preprint, 12 Nov 2025.
COVERAGE: FULL. Read all of the /tmp extraction (1066 lines, 17 pages), including limitations, Table 6 and Appendix B. pypdf reported 60780 chars. References were skimmed for origins only.

CENTRAL CLAIM: TiDAR drafts tokens with one-step diffusion and verifies them autoregressively in the same forward pass, using a structured attention mask. It puts the "free token slots" of memory-bound decoding to use. The authors say it is the first architecture to close the quality gap with AR while giving much higher tokens per second than AR and than EAGLE-3 speculative decoding.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Claim: Decode is memory-bound at small batch, so extra token slots per forward cost almost no latency until the model turns compute-bound.
 number: none (latency flat over a range of token slots; the axis is log, 10^0 to 10^2)
 setup: Qwen3-32B decoding, H100, batch size 1, FlashAttention 2, past KV lengths 1024/2048/4096 (Fig 1).
 quote: "Latency stays relatively the same with a certain amount of tokens sent to forward (free + cheap token slots), before transitioning to the compute-bound regime."
 where: p3, Fig 1 caption
2. Claim: Headline wall-clock speedup, 4.71x (1.5B) and 5.91x (8B) over the same-size AR baseline, with comparable quality.
 number: 4.71x; 5.91x
 setup: single H100, batch size 1, prompts from the downstream generative tasks, native PyTorch with Flex Attention, BF16, exact KV cache for all models. Baselines: Qwen2.5 1.5B Base for the 1.5B model, Qwen3 8B Base for the 8B model. Speedup is tokens/s relative to the AR baseline, averaged over the tasks.
 quote: "TiDAR 1.5B can achieve an average of 4.71x relative speedup to Qwen2.5 1.5B in terms of decoding throughput and TiDAR 8B with an average of 5.91x over Qwen3 8B while maintaining comparable performances."
 where: p9, section 4.3
3. Claim: Tokens per forward (T/NFE) is high.
 number: 7.45 (1.5B avg), 8.25 (8B, trust diffusion), 8.23 (8B, trust AR)
 setup: Table 2 averages over HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP, MBPP+, GSM8K, Minerva Math. T/NFE means average tokens produced per network function evaluation (one model forward). 1.5B uses block sizes 4/8/16 in Fig 4; 8B uses block size 16.
 quote: "TiDAR 1.5B ⋆ 43.29% 39.02% 41.40% 61.11% 53.90% 25.48% 44.03% (6.50) (6.50) (9.25) (9.43) (5.07) (7.92) (7.45)"
 where: p9, Table 2
4. Claim: Quality against same-size AR. TiDAR 1.5B averages 44.03% against 41.64% for Qwen2.5 1.5B, its initialisation. TiDAR 8B averages 63.90% (Trust AR) and 65.31% (Trust Diff) against 68.09% for Qwen3 8B.
 number: 44.03 vs 41.64; 65.31 / 63.90 vs 68.09 (generative average)
 setup: Table 2, lm_eval_harness 0.4.8, task configs in Table 6 (HumanEval/HumanEval+ 0-shot, 512 gen length, Pass@1; MBPP/MBPP+ 3-shot, 512, Pass@1; GSM8K-CoT 8-shot, 256, strict-match; Minerva Math 4-shot, 512, exact-match). TiDAR 1.5B is initialised from Qwen2.5 1.5B, continually pretrained on 50B tokens. TiDAR 8B is initialised from Qwen3 8B, on 150B tokens, block size 16.
 quote: "Qwen2.5 1.5B 35.98% 29.88% 43.60% 59.23% 54.74% 26.40% 41.64%" and "TiDAR (Trust Diff) 8B‡ 57.93% 55.49% 65.40% 80.95% 80.44% 51.64% 65.31% (7.30) (7.29) (10.00) (10.13) (7.07) (7.68) (8.25)"
 where: p9, Table 2
 note: the abstract's "close the quality gap" holds for 1.5B (the paper calls it "lossless") and is "minimal loss" for 8B. The 8B gap is about 2.8 points (Trust Diff) to 4.2 points (Trust AR).
5. Claim: TiDAR beats the Block Diffusion baseline, Dream and LLaDA on generative quality. Block Diff 1.5B averages 38.41% and Block Diff 4B 60.27%. Dream 7B averages 58.74% and LLaDA 8B 41.78%. Dream, LLaDA and Block Diff are decoded at one token per forward there, so their T/NFE is 1.
 number: see the figures above
 setup: Block Diff was trained by the authors with the same recipe. Dream and LLaDA are public weights.
 quote: "For all diffusion models we decode one token per forward for the best quality and report the average number of tokens (T/NFE) generated by TiDAR in parenthesis."
 where: p9, Table 2 caption
6. Claim: TiDAR beats EAGLE-3 in measured throughput; its T/NFE is higher and so is its T/NFE to T/s conversion.
 number: EAGLE-3 speedup values appear only inside Fig 4 as plotted points (extraction is ambiguous; I did not attribute them)
 setup: EAGLE-3 uses public weights from AngelSlim and Tengyunw on Qwen3-8B Instruct, because no weights exist for the base model. Single H100, batch size 1.
 quote: "we show that our raw acceptance rate (T/NFE) is higher than those of EAGLE-3 open weights, and more importantly, our conversion rate (from T/NFE to T/s) is higher, thanks to the parallel drafting and sampling with a single model forward."
 where: p9
7. Claim: Likelihood tasks. The AR mode (pure causal mask) computes likelihood like an AR model in a single NFE, so there is no Monte Carlo estimate.
 number: TiDAR 1.5B avg 64.43% (Qwen2.5 1.5B 65.16%); TiDAR 8B avg 75.40% (Qwen3 8B 74.25%)
 setup: MMLU 5-shot, ARC-e, ARC-c, Hellaswag, PIQA, Winogrande 5-shot. Block Diff, Dream and LLaDA use MC with 128 steps.
 quote: "TiDAR 8B ‡ 76.57% 84.18% 58.53% 76.36% 80.25% 76.48% 75.40%"
 where: p10, Table 3
8. Claim: Decoding-strategy ablation. The TiDAR rows are on full-mask models, 1.5B. TiDAR gets higher T/NFE and higher scores than confidence-threshold decoding, which loses quality as parallelism rises.
 number: TiDAR 4 drafts T/NFE 3.47 (HumanEval 38.42%); 16 drafts 6.97 (41.16%). Confidence >0.6 gives T/NFE 3.81 with HumanEval 22.56%. Confidence max (1 token/NFE) gives 34.45% on HumanEval.
 quote: "TiDAR (4 drafts) 3.47 38.42% 50.96% 55.87%"
 where: p11, Table 4
9. Claim: Full-mask training beats random-mask training.
 number: Avg 48.42% vs 45.45% at draft 4; 48.94% vs 45.68% at draft 8. T/NFE 3.47 vs 3.42, and 5.49 vs 5.22.
 setup: 1.5B, HumanEval/MBPP/GSM8K averages.
 quote: "Full 4 38.42% 50.96% 55.87% 48.42% (3.46) (3.72) (3.23) (3.47)"
 where: p12, Table 5
10. Claim: Same-recipe Pareto (1.5B, 50B tokens). TiDAR beats Block Diffusion, but a gap to the fine-tuned AR model remains.
 number: "7x more tokens per NFE"
 quote: "Our model achieves the best Pareto Frontier compared to Block Diffusion and AR and is approaching the quality of fine-tuned AR with 7x more tokens per NFE."
 where: p11, Fig 5 caption. Also: "We also notice the remaining quality gap from the fine-tuned AR models, which we believe could be potentially closed with more data".
11. Claim: Sampling with AR or diffusion logits makes little difference. The mixing rule is argmax of beta*logits_ar + (1-beta)*logits_diff.
 number: none
 quote: "This also indicates that it is the autoregressive rejection sampling that guarantees the quality-speedup trade-offs rather than the AR knowledge."
 where: p11-12, section 4.3.3 and Fig 6. The paper's section numbering is 4.4.3.

MECHANISM (for notes)
- Each forward splits into three sections: the prefix, whose KV cache is reused; the draft tokens from the last step, which are verified by AR rejection sampling under causal attention; and mask tokens, which pre-draft the next step in one-step diffusion, bidirectional within the block, conditioned on all possible accept lengths.
- The draft model is the base model itself.
- Rejected tokens' KV entries are evicted. No KV recompute occurs.
- Training sequence length is doubled by appending an all-mask copy.
- Loss: (1/(1+alpha)) * (alpha * L_AR + L_Diff), with alpha=1 in most runs. Labels are shifted for AR and aligned for diffusion.
- Inference needs no hyperparameters.
- Table 1 compares TiDAR with classic speculative decoding, APD, EAGLE-3/DeepSeek-V3 MTP and Apple MTP on three axes: drafter shared with base, drafting capacity, and drafting parallel to verification.

LIMITS
- All speed numbers are batch size 1 on one H100, in native PyTorch with Flex Attention. The authors concede that large-batch behaviour is not benchmarked: "Although we focus on batch size = 1 efficiency benchmarking, it does not mean that TiDAR cannot handle large batch size." They only assert that the block length can be adjusted zero-shot and that "FLOPs / token" is competitive; no data are shown. At larger batch sizes decode becomes compute-bound and the free-slot premise weakens. The paper does not test this.
- The Fig 1 profile uses Qwen3-32B, but no TiDAR model is that size. Only 1.5B and 8B are evaluated, with the 8B at block size 16 only.
- No variance, seeds or confidence intervals appear anywhere. Each result is a single run.
- The authors state that speculative decoding "is able to guarantee exactly the same output as the base model", and TiDAR does not carry that guarantee. TiDAR needs continual pretraining (50B and 150B tokens) and is a new model, not a drop-in for an existing one.
- The EAGLE-3 comparison uses the Instruct model with third-party weights, and TiDAR 8B is a Base-derived model. The pairing is not matched.
- The 8B model is below Qwen3 8B on the generative average (see claim 4).
- Training needs doubled sequence length. Long-context extension is untested (max training length 4096) and deferred to future work.
- Evaluation is code, math and multiple-choice only. Generation lengths are 256-512 tokens. There are no chat, long-form or reasoning-model evaluations.
- The paper gives no memory or FLOPs overhead numbers, and no throughput table (speedups appear only in Fig 4).
- The authors concede that custom kernels and scheduling were not done.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- Speculative decoding: Leviathan, Kalman, Matias 2023 (ref 11); Chen et al. 2023 (ref 16, speculative sampling).
- Draft heads and drafters: Medusa (Cai et al. 2024); EAGLE, EAGLE-2, EAGLE-3 (Li et al. 2024/2025); DeepSeek-V3 MTP (2024); Apple MTP "Your LLM knows the future" (Samragh et al. 2025), cited as the inspiration for pre-drafting conditioned on all possible rejection outcomes; Gloeckle et al. 2024 (multi-token prediction).
- Block Diffusion: Arriola et al. 2025. TiDAR keeps only the last block bidirectional.
- Set Block Decoding: Gat et al. 2025, for the doubled-sequence training.
- Sequential diffusion LMs: Liu et al. 2025, for one-step diffusion drafting.
- Diffusion LMs: LLaDA (Nie et al. 2025), Dream (Ye et al. 2025), MDLM (Sahoo et al. 2024), Fast-dLLM v1/v2 (Wu et al. 2025), d-KV cache (Ma et al. 2025), APD (Israel et al. 2025).
- Systems: FlashAttention, Flex Attention (Dong et al. 2024), PagedAttention (Kwon et al. 2023); the memory-bound view cites Yuan et al. 2024 (roofline survey).

CODE: none in the paper. The only code-like detail is footnote 1: "q_len = block_len·(1 + block_len)", the query length per decode step for the precomputed mask slice.

FIGURES (checked from captions in the extraction, not rendered)
- Fig 1 (p3): latency against token slots for Qwen3-32B on H100 at batch size 1. Shows the "free token slots" idea. It is the best figure for the "why decode leaves compute idle" section.
- Fig 2 (p5): TiDAR architecture, one forward containing prefix, last-step drafts being verified and pre-drafts for the next step, with draft length 3 and accepted length 2.
- Fig 3 (p5): training and decoding attention masks.
- Fig 4 (p7): speed-quality scatter against AR, EAGLE-3 and Block Diffusion at 1.5B and 8B, with T/NFE labels. Main result.
- Fig 5 (p11): Pareto frontier at 1.5B under the same recipe.
- Fig 6 (p12): trust-AR ratio sweep.
- Fig 7 (p17): prefill mask.
- Tables: Table 1 (p3) on speculative frameworks, Table 2 (p9) on generative results, Table 4 (p11) on decoding strategies.

PROBLEMS
- The extraction mangles Fig 4 axis labels and some table rows, and the EAGLE-3 point values in Fig 4 cannot be separated cleanly. The Table 2 and Table 5 numbers above are copied exactly.
- The extraction's first line reads "17 pages" and "2025-11-13", a banner artefact, and not a title.
- The text says "Section 4.4.3" for the trust AR/diffusion discussion, but the numbering at that point is 4.4.3. Section 4.2.1 also refers to "Section 4.4.3" for the trust-AR choice, which is consistent.
- No embedded instructions were found.
